payload.name: wavelet-packet
payload.scope: A human-made signal decomposition method that generalizes the wavelet transform by decomposing both approximation and detail subbands at each tree level, producing a complete binary tree of subband representations. Unlike the standard wavelet transform that only recursively decomposes the approximation branch, the wavelet-packet algorithm applies the same decomposition to every node, enabling optimal basis selection for signal-specific energy concentration.

definition.body: A signal decomposition algorithm that recursively partitions a signal into subbands using a binary tree structure. At each node, both the low-frequency (approximation) and high-frequency (detail) outputs are further decomposed by a pair of quadrature mirror filters followed by downsampling. The algorithm is parameterized by: (1) the maximum decomposition depth (number of tree levels), (2) the wavelet basis function (e.g., Daubechies, Haar, Coiflet) defining the filter coefficients, (3) the node selection criteria (e.g., best-first, bottom-up, or exhaustive search over the full tree), and (4) the cost function for optimal basis selection (commonly Shannon entropy of subband energies). The persistence mechanism is algorithmic: the method is implemented in DSP libraries (MATLAB Wavelet Toolbox, Python PyWavelets, librosa) and taught in signal processing curricula. e.g.: MATLAB Wavelet Toolbox wavedec2 function; PyWavelets pywt.wavedec with full tree decomposition; librosa.feature.melspectrogram using packet decomposition for audio feature extraction | not: standard discrete wavelet transform (only approximations decomposed, not the full tree) [formal: transformatio pacellae waveleticae | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes]

payload.name: gabor-transform
payload.scope: A human-made time-frequency analysis method that computes the short-time Fourier transform using a fixed Gaussian window function. Introduced by Dennis Gabor in 1946 as a 'deterministic uncertainty principle' for signal analysis, it produces a complex-valued representation of signal energy localized in both time and frequency. Unlike the general STFT where window shape and width are free parameters, the Gabor transform uses a specifically Gaussian window whose width parameter sigma controls the time-frequency resolution trade-off.

definition.body: A time-frequency representation defined by G(tau, omega) = integral from -inf to +inf of f(t) * exp(-(t-tau)^2/(2*sigma^2)) * exp(-i*omega*t) dt, where sigma is the Gaussian window width parameter controlling the time-frequency resolution trade-off. Parameters: (1) sigma — the standard deviation of the Gaussian window, determining the fixed time-frequency resolution bandwidth (Heisenberg box size = sigma * (1/(4*pi*sigma))), (2) the time and frequency sampling step sizes for discrete computation. The persistence mechanism is algorithmic and theoretical: implemented in MATLAB (gabor), Python (scipy.signal.gaussian for window generation), and image processing toolboxes; foundational to squeezed-state quantum mechanics and the Gabor frame theory of Daubechies, Grossmann, and Meyer. e.g.: MATLAB gabor function for image feature extraction; Python librosa.feature.melspectrogram using fixed Gaussian windows; Daubechies Grossmann Meyer Gabor frame theory in applied harmonic analysis textbooks | not: short-time Fourier transform with non-Gaussian window (e.g., rectangular, Hanning, Blackman windows) [formal: gaboriana transformatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes]
